column1: # ISO_ACCEPTS.tsv -- PAT rejection-named tests (iso7185prt*) that carry NO ISO 7185 violation and that the oracle ACCEPTS, so each is
# graded as an ACCEPTANCE test: PASS when SCRIP prints fpc -Miso's output in both modes (cut live by test_pascal_pat_suite.sh, like the
# iso7185pat* population), FAIL otherwise, IN the denominator. Ruled by the ceo, CEO-1269 (2026-09-25), superseding CEO-1231's OUTSIDE
# ruling for these two; measured by the ceo 15:4x: fpc -Miso accepts both and runs both rc 0.
# Columns: program <TAB> the oracle measurement <TAB> why ISO 7185 does not refuse it

column2: fpc -Miso rc 0, prints 1 to 10 (one per line, width 11)
column3: label 1 is declared and prefixes exactly one statement (ISO 7185 6.2.1/6.8.1); nothing requires a goto to it

column2: fpc -Miso rc 0, prints nothing (compile-time note for the unused i)
column3: a declared, never-used variable violates no clause; the test's own header calls it a compiler quality test

column2: fpc -Miso rc 0, prints "The result is: false" (the same under -Cr; ceo, 2026-09-26 08:16, CEO-1274)
column3: ISO 7185 6.7.2.1 leaves the evaluation of the second operand of and/or implementation-dependent; the oracle short-circuits, so a[11] is never evaluated and no 6.5.3.2 error occurs (SCRIP short-circuits likewise since this landing)

column2: fpc -Miso rc 0, prints " 1.0e+000" (no newline; the floating-point form's minimum width, the exponent letter e at every width -- str_real_iso; ceo CEO-1301)
column3: ISO 7185 6.9.3.1 makes a TotalWidth below one an error, and 3.2 lets an implementation leave an error undetected; the oracle does, so the program is inside the baseline and is graded on the oracle's output

column2: fpc -Miso rc 0, prints "1" (no newline; a FracDigits of zero writes no point and no fraction)
column3: ISO 7185 6.9.3.1 makes a FracDigits below one an error, and 3.2 lets an implementation leave an error undetected; the oracle does (ceo CEO-1301)

column2: fpc -Miso rc 0, prints "1" (an integer written with a TotalWidth of zero takes the width it needs)
column3: ISO 7185 6.9.3.1 makes a TotalWidth below one an error, and 3.2 lets an implementation leave an error undetected; the oracle does (ceo CEO-1301)

column2: fpc -Miso rc 0, prints "1" (a FracDigits of zero writes no point and no fraction)
column3: ISO 7185 6.9.3.1 makes a FracDigits below one an error, and 3.2 lets an implementation leave an error undetected; the oracle does (ceo CEO-1301)

column2: fpc -Miso rc 0, prints "0" (an integer written with the default width: ten spaces and a 0, no newline); SCRIP prints the same in both modes
column3: ISO 7185 6.7.1 makes a use of an undefined variable an error, and 3.2 lets an implementation leave an error undetected; the oracle does, and the program's own header says it tests whether a processor checks undefines ("Not many compilers check for undefines") (ceo CEO-1301 precedent for 1758a, 1758b, 1839, 1840; cfo, 2026-10-09)

column2: fpc -Miso rc 0, prints nothing; SCRIP prints the same in both modes
column3: ISO 7185 6.5.3.3 makes a read of an undiscriminated variant after a write of another arm an error, and 3.2 lets an implementation leave an error undetected; the oracle does, and the program prints nothing (ceo, the cfo concurring, CEO-1575, on the CEO-1301 precedent)

column2: fpc -Miso rc 0, prints "i: 99" (the integer written with the default width; the oracle passes the address of the variant arm a.i, so the write of the other arm a.c is seen through the formal); SCRIP prints the same in both modes since a var actual that is a component is the component itself and a variant field a view of the record's byte region (SCRIP 9695845d1, a445379ea)
column3: ISO 7185 6.5.3.3 case D makes a write of an undiscriminated variant while a reference to another arm exists an error, and 3.2 lets an implementation leave an error undetected; the oracle does and the program runs to a definite answer, so it is graded by output against the oracle, in the denominator (ceo CEO-1575: not ungradable, not detect-at-the-call)
